viva.question: Why is only 'finite' intersection required, not arbitrary intersection?
viva.answer: Arbitrary intersections of open sets in familiar spaces can collapse to single points, which are not open.
viva.why: Requiring arbitrary intersection-closure would make almost no interesting topology satisfy the axioms.
viva.followUp: Give an explicit example where an infinite intersection of open sets is not open.
viva.trap: Assuming intersections behave exactly like unions in the axioms.

viva.question: Can a point be in a set without being one of its limit points?
viva.answer: Yes — an isolated point of A is a standard example.
viva.why: The definition of a limit point requires OTHER points of A nearby, not just membership itself.
viva.followUp: Is every point of a finite set a limit point of that set?
viva.trap: Confusing 'p \in A' with 'p is a limit point of A'.
